articles.standfirst: Guia de Compras testou Jovi X300 Ultra e Oppo Find X9 Pro, modelos superpremium com câmeras assinadas por Zeiss e Hasselblad, bateria duradoura e alto desempenho.
articles.summary: Guia de Compras testou Jovi X300 Ultra e Oppo Find X9 Pro, modelos superpremium com câmeras assinadas por Zeiss e Hasselblad, bateria duradoura e alto desempenho.
articles.body:
Jovi X300 Ultra (à esquerda) e Oppo Find X9 Pro (à direita) — Foto: Henrique Martin/g1

As fabricantes chinesas Jovi e Oppo lançaram recentemente seus primeiros celulares premium: o X300 Ultra e o Find X9 Pro, que estão entre as melhores câmeras portáteis disponíveis em 2026.

📸 Só que, para garantir o “pedigree" de marcas famosas da fotografia presentes nos aparelhos — Zeiss, no Jovi, e Hasselblad, no Oppo —, o consumidor precisa fazer um alto investimento.

🤑 O modelo da Oppo é mais "econômico" na comparação e pode ser encontrado na faixa de R$ 11,5 mil.

💰 Já o da Jovi sai por R$ 20 mil, um dos mais caros à venda , mas vem em um kit luxuoso com acessórios que incluem lentes adicionais, capa e um suporte com bateria extra.

Além das câmeras, ambos apresentam desempenho excepcional de última geração e baterias que duram muito tempo longe da tomada. Ambos rodam Android 16 , uma das versões mais recentes do sistema do Google.

O Guia de Compras testou os dois aparelhos nas últimas semanas e mostra os resultados a seguir. Os celulares foram enviados por empréstimo e serão devolvidos aos fabricantes.

O Jovi X300 Ultra é um aparelho para poucos, não só pelo preço.

É um celular voltado a um público de nicho – interessado em fotografia quase profissional em um aparelho que cabe (apertado) no bolso.

Se comparar apenas nas configurações técnicas, ele concorre com o Oppo Find X9 Pro, mas também com iPhone 17 Pro , Galaxy S26 Ultra e Motorola Signature .

Detalhe da câmera traseira do Jovi X300 Ultra — Foto: Henrique Martin/g1

A única diferença mesmo é que os concorrentes não têm um kit tão completo como o da Jovi disponível no mercado brasileiro. A caixa vem com:

Dois extensores de telefoto , um de 200 mm (equivalente a zoom óptico de 2,35x), e um de 400 mm (4,7x). É como se fosse uma versão miniatura das lentes usadas nas câmeras profissionais.

Uma capa protetora de alumínio com suporte para encaixar as lentes ou filtros.

Uma empunhadura com disparador, que ainda tem uma bateria extra (2.300 mAh) para alimentar o telefone.

Alça de transporte, anéis para o encaixe de filtros e suporte para tripé nas lentes.

Jovi X300 Ultra e todos seus acessórios — Foto: Divulgação

O Jovi X300 Ultra é um modelo parrudo de smartphone e é bastante pesado (237 g) sem os acessórios, um pouco a mais que o Find X9 Pro (224 g).

As opções de cores são "preto volcano" e "verde sálvia".

A fabricante chinesa Oppo oferece, no exterior, um kit com acessórios da Hasselblad para o Find X9 Pro. A companhia optou por não vender esse pacote extra no Brasil.

Segundo a Oppo, a ausência dos extras tem a ver com a "estratégia de portfólio" para o país e "que a empresa está priorizando produtos e acessórios que estejam mais alinhados ao perfil e às necessidades dos consumidores locais".

Dito isso, nada de kit para quem comprar o Find X9 Pro por aqui. Em sites de importação da China, é possível encontrar o item na faixa dos R$ 1.600, sem contar os impostos.

Por conta disso, na parte de câmeras, foram comparadas somente as lentes principais dos aparelhos, desconsiderando os acessórios do X300 Ultra ( clique aqui para ler mais sobre eles ).

O Oppo Find X9 Pro está disponível nas cores branco e "titânio grafite".

Detalhe da câmera traseira do Oppo Find X9 Pro — Foto: Henrique Martin/g1

O Jovi X300 Ultra usa o chip mais recente da Qualcomm, o Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 de 3 nanômetros.

Já o modelo da Oppo é equipado com o processador da MediaTek, o Dimensity 9500, também de 3 nanômetros ( entenda por que isso é importante ).

Apesar de terem fornecedores distintos, o smartphone da Jovi foi um pouco mais veloz que o da Oppo na maioria dos testes, que avaliam o uso simulado do aparelho no dia a dia.

O comportamento mais rápido do Jovi se repetiu nos testes de desempenho gráfico com games e vídeos.

De qualquer forma, nenhum dos dois aparelhos ficou lento ou travou durante o uso. Vale notar que ambos contam com 16 GB de memória RAM e 512 GB de armazenamento interno.

Os dois celulares podem passar bastante tempo longe da tomada graças às grandes capacidades de carga. Ambos usam baterias de silício-carbono, uma tecnologia mais recente no mercado.

O Jovi X300 Ultra tem 6.600 mAh de capacidade, enquanto o Oppo Find X9 Pro conta com 7.500 mAh. Durante os testes, o modelo da Oppo mostrou que consegue ficar mais de 26 horas longe da tomada . O aparelho da Jovi alcançou 27 horas .

A diferença entre os tempos de uso, mesmo com capacidades distintas, ocorre pela forma como cada fabricante otimiza o sistema operacional para economizar energia. Caso seja necessário, é possível ativar o modo de economia nos dois aparelhos.

É importante ressaltar que cada pessoa tem um padrão de uso específico. Na prática, a duração da bateria pode variar conforme as tarefas executadas no dia a dia.

O Jovi X300 Ultra tem quatro lentes na traseira: duas com 200 megapixels de resolução (principal e telefoto com zoom de 3,7x) e uma de 50 MP (grande angular).

A quarta lente não fotografa : é apenas um sensor para ajudar no ajuste de cores das imagens. O equipamento conta ainda com um chip VS1+, dedicado para o processamento de fotos.

Já o Oppo Find X9 Pro traz 200 megapixels no zoom de 3x e dois sensores de 50 MP (grande angular e principal), sem o sensor extra do concorrente.

Nos dois, a câmera de selfie é de 50 megapixels.

Os resultados em ambos são excelentes. As opções dos dois aparelhos permitem ajustes finos para o fotógrafo e uso de filtros das marcas parceiras (Zeiss e Hasselblad).

Tudo isso deixa o fotógrafo com maior controle sobre o resultado, como nesse modo macro do rosto do gato (abaixo).

Foto em macro: Jovi X300 Ultra (à esquerda) e Oppo Find X9 Pro (à direita) — Foto: Henrique Martin/g1

Uma percepção rápida sobre o Jovi X300 Ultra é que os resultados salvos na galeria da câmera têm pouca ou quase nenhuma alteração automática na comparação com o da Oppo.

Isso significa que, apesar das lentes e filtros, o X300 Ultra realiza menos o chamado "pós-processamento" da imagem (o que algumas marcas podem dizer que é "inteligência artificial" e está presente nos celulares desde antes de o termo se popularizar).

O da Oppo usa mais pós-processamento. Isso não é ruim, mas mostra que a Jovi quer mesmo deixar o controle nas mãos do fotógrafo para uma edição/ajuste posterior.

Isso é bastante visível em outra foto macro:

Ou em um zoom nas fontes do Museu do Ipiranga, em São Paulo:

Zoom: Jovi X300 Ultra (em cima) e Oppo Find X9 Pro (embaixo) — Foto: Henrique Martin/g1

E até mesmo em fotos em modo retrato, com o fundo desfocado.

Modo retrato: Jovi X300 Ultra (à esquerda) e Oppo Find X9 Pro (à direita) — Foto: Henrique Martin/g1

As fotos diurnas em resolução máxima, com 200 MP de definição, fornecem muito detalhes de perto , mesmo a uma longa distância:

Zoom em resolução máxima: Jovi X300 Ultra (em cima) e Oppo Find X9 Pro (embaixo) — Foto: Henrique Martin/g1

E captam muitos detalhes na resolução padrão também:

Foto diurna: Jovi X300 Ultra (em cima) e Oppo Find X9 Pro (embaixo) — Foto: Henrique Martin/g1

Nas fotos noturnas, resultados excelentes continuaram a aparecer.

Foto noturna: Jovi X300 Ultra (acima) e Oppo Find X9 Pro (abaixo) — Foto: Henrique Martin/g1

A única diferença é que o Jovi X300 Ultra conseguiu fotografar a Lua nessa noite com o zoom híbrido, mas o Oppo Find X9 Pro, não.

Foto noturna: Lua capturada pelo Jovi X300 Ultra — Foto: Henrique Martin/g1

A câmera de selfies dos dois aparelhos é ótima. O fotógrafo só se esqueceu de desativar o modo retrato em uma delas e o espelhamento automático em outra 🤓.

Selfie com a câmera frontal: Jovi X300 Ultra (à esquerda) e Oppo Find X9 Pro (à direita) — Foto: Henrique Martin/g1

Os dois aparelhos do teste são a primeira tentativa das suas fabricantes em lançar aparelhos no segmento mais caro dos celulares.

Nesse sentido, Jovi e Oppo acertaram com aparelhos de desempenho e baterias excelentes e câmeras excepcionais.

O Jovi vai para quem procura o máximo em fotografia e está disposto a pagar mais com o kit. O Oppo já é uma escolha mais racional para quem quer qualidade equivalente por menos.

Estão no mesmo nível de concorrentes mais populares no país, como Galaxy S26 Ultra, da Samsung, e o Moto Signature, da Motorola.

Só que ainda são bem mais caros que os rivais, por conta do "pedigree" de seus parceiros fotográficos. O S26 Ultra já está na faixa dos R$ 8.000, e o Moto Signature, R$ 6.000.

Câmera e acessórios: conta com lentes da marca Zeiss e é vendido por R$ 20 mil em um kit luxuoso, que inclui lentes adicionais, capa e suporte com bateria extra.

Desempenho superior: equipado com o chip Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 (3 nanômetros), foi ligeiramente mais rápido que o concorrente nos testes de uso diário, vídeos e games.

Autonomia de bateria: possui bateria de silício-carbono de 6.600 mAh que, graças à otimização do sistema, alcançou 27 horas de duração nos testes.

Câmera e custo-benefício: traz lentes da famosa marca Hasselblad e é a opção mais econômica do comparativo, encontrado na faixa de R$ 11,5 mil, mas não tem o kit adicional.

Processamento: usa o chip MediaTek Dimensity 9500 (3 nanômetros), garantindo um funcionamento fluido, sem lentidão ou travamentos.

Maior capacidade de carga: sua bateria de silício-carbono tem 7.500 mAh de capacidade nominal e conseguiu ficar mais de 26 horas longe da tomada durante os testes.

Para os testes de desempenho, foram utilizados três aplicativos: PC Mark e 3D Mark, da UL Laboratories, e o GeekBench 6/7, da Primate Labs. Eles simulam tarefas cotidianas dos smartphones, como processamento de imagens, edição de textos, duração de bateria e navegação na web, entre outros.

Esses testes rodam em várias plataformas – como Android, iOS, Windows e MacOS – e permitem comparar o desempenho entre elas, criando um padrão para essa comparação.

Para as avaliações de bateria, as telas dos smartphones ficaram com o brilho automático ativado, com o teste em luz ambiente durante o dia.

A bateria foi carregada a 100% e o teste rodou por horas até atingir 20% de carga, quando é interrompido e mostra a duração estimada em horas/minutos.

articles.title: Your white T-shirt shouldn't be see-through. Fashion experts explain what to look for.
articles.summary: Before you buy another white tee that shows too much, we asked stylists to explain how to spot one with real coverage.
articles.body:
Our experts independently review everything we recommend. If you buy through our links, we may earn commission.

I've never put on a white T-shirt and thought, "Great, I hope everyone can see exactly what's happening underneath this." To be fair, not every white tee has to be a centerpiece: If you're buying undershirts in bulk to wear under suits or sweaters, a thinner fabric can make sense. But when the white T-shirt is the outfit — or at least a visible part of it — it has to have enough weight, structure and coverage to hold its own.

"Some transparency can absolutely be intentional, especially now that sheer and 'naked dressing' have become such visible fashion conversations," says fashion stylist Aricia Symes , founder of Unfoldid. "The issue is expectation. If you are buying a tee to be a clean everyday white T-shirt, it should have enough coverage to stand on its own."

Here's what to look for so you can know what you're getting, return fewer sad shirts and keep accidental transparency to a minimum. We've also included examples below, featuring some tested picks from our guides to the best white T-shirts for men and the best white T-shirts for women .

The more expensive the shirt, the better the opacity, right? Wrong, pros say. Price can be a clue, but it only gets you so far. Some expensive white tees are soft, thin and drapey, while some affordable ones have surprisingly solid coverage.

"I don't think price is a reliable indicator of whether a white T-shirt will be opaque," says Dina Cerchione , stylist at DMC Styles. "I've worked with clothing at every price point for 30 years, and I've seen expensive tees that are super thin and feel cheap and inexpensive ones that are great. Sometimes you're paying for better materials and construction and sometimes you're just paying for the label."

And don't trust the brand name alone. "The brand matters less than choosing the right version within the brand," Symes says. "Even the same retailer may sell a tissue tee, a fitted rib tee and a heavier everyday tee, and those are going to behave very differently in white."

Quality is still important, just in a more boring and useful way than considering the price tag alone. Cerchione says to look at the neckline first, since "a crewneck rib should spring back into place when you gently stretch it." Straight stitching, flat hems and double-needle stitching are also details she looks for in a well-made tee.

Abercrombie & Fitch Seamless Fabric Baby Tee

Fiber content matters, but it doesn't tell you everything. A tag that says 100% cotton sounds reassuring, but cotton can be thin, thick, tightly knit, loose, smooth or slubby — and all of that can affect how much shows through. It usually comes down to weight, yarn, knit density and how much the fabric stretches once it's actually on your body.

"100% cotton is usually my first choice," Cerchione says. "It's breathable, comfortable, durable and a good cotton jersey has the structure I like in a classic men's tee." For someone who wants a white tee to wear on its own, she recommends a "medium-to-substantial-weight cotton or cotton-rich blend with a dense knit and enough room that it isn't pulling across the body."

Turner Allen , a men's personal stylist, also puts cotton first. "If your goal is to find a white T-shirt that won't leave you feeling exposed, I'd prioritize 100% cotton in a medium-to-heavy weight with a dense knit," he says.

Cotton blends can work too, especially when cotton is still doing most of the work. Cerchione says a little polyester can add durability, wrinkle resistance and help a shirt keep its shape, though too much can start to read more like performance wear. She's more cautious with modal, rayon and viscose in white because they tend to be softer and drapier, which can make them less forgiving.

Abercrombie & Fitch Premium Heavyweight Cropped Tee

Rosemia Oversized Crewneck T-Shirt for Men

Quince 100% Organic Cotton Boxy V-Neck Tee

Fit matters because pulling changes the fabric. "A shirt may seem solid on the hanger, but once the fabric pulls across the chest, shoulders or stomach, the knit opens up and lets more light through," Symes says. Translation: It can become see-through exactly where you least want it to.

Luckily, there are some specific cuts that can help. Allen recommends avoiding T-shirts that are too fitted or clingy when sheerness is a concern. "Instead, opt for a slightly relaxed or boxy fit to ensure the fabric moves independently of the body," he says.

Cerchione likes classic and relaxed fits for the same reason. They tend to be more forgiving because the fabric isn't stretched so hard across the body. And no, that doesn't mean slim, fitted or shrunken tees are off the table if those are your go-tos. They just need a better fabric behind them.

The easiest way to think about it is in terms of tension. If the shirt skims the body, it has a much better shot at staying opaque. A closer fit in compact cotton can look clean and intentional, while a closer fit in a very thin rib, loose slub or lightweight jersey is more likely to show through because the fabric has less room to hold its coverage once it starts pulling across the body.

"The best opacity test is daylight," Symes says. "Fitting room lighting can be forgiving, and store lighting does not always reveal sheerness the way natural light does." If you're shopping in person, step toward a window or brighter part of the store if you can and make sure you check the shirt on your body, especially where the fabric is under the most tension.

Universal Thread Women's Vintage Jersey Crewneck T-Shirt

"A white T-shirt is not automatically more opaque just because it feels thicker," Symes says. "Density is usually the bigger issue." In normal-person terms, the threads need to be packed closely enough that light, skin and everything else underneath aren't immediately part of the conversation.

"Knit density is really about how closely the yarns are packed together, not just how thick the shirt feels," Cerchione adds. "The tighter the knit, the less space there is for light and skin to show through."

For white tees, she says dense jersey and interlock are generally better bets for coverage. Tissue-weight fabrics, slub, very drapey knits and looser constructions tend to let more light through. Rib can be sneaky too, as it may look solid at first, then stretch across the body and suddenly get a lot less discreet.

Symes also says not to pay for softness alone. A white tee should feel good, obviously, but it needs enough body to look clean once it's on. A shirt that feels incredible in the package but gives up the second it stretches isn't doing you any favors.

A New Day Women's Short Sleeve Perfect T-Shirt

Hanes Women's Perfect-T Short Sleeve T-Shirt

The pros say there are some words that should make you more confident when shopping online. "'Midweight,' 'heavyweight,' 'dense,' 'compact,' 'structured jersey,' 'interlock knit' or 'double-knit' usually make me more confident that a white tee will give better coverage," Symes says.

On the other hand, there are words that should make you pause. Symes says some of those are "tissue," "burnout," "sheer," "semi-sheer," "featherweight," "airy" and "drapey." If a shirt keeps being described as "barely there," "perfect for layering" or "invisible under clothes," believe it. While this can be ideal if you want something to wear under a button-down or you're intentionally going for a little transparency, it's probably a sign to keep browsing when coverage is the goal.

Also, read the photos critically, because they may not tell you the whole story. Cerchione says she wants to see the white T-shirt "on a body and worn by itself, not just a photo of the tee." A white tee styled under a jacket, tucked into shadow or photographed from one perfect angle is only telling you so much. You should look closely at the chest, neckline and wherever the fabric stretches. Reviews can help too, especially if shoppers use words like sheer, see-through, thin or transparent.

Gildan Heavy Cotton Adult T-Shirt, 2-Pack

Amazon Essentials Men's Relaxed-Fit Heavyweight Cotton T-Shirt

When you think "white tee," you might think of the stark-white multi-packs you've reached for in bulk. But those bright whites can create more contrast with skin, chest hair, bras, undershirts or anything else underneath, making a shirt appear more revealing.

Allen says bright, optic white T-shirts often have a cool blue undertone, which can make them contrast against most skin tones. "Instead, consider a soft off-white or subtle cream," he says. "These shades have warmer, softer undertones that tend to create less contrast against the skin, resulting in a more natural and forgiving appearance."

Cerchione agrees that the shade of white can affect how revealing a T-shirt appears, even though fabric is still the biggest factor. She says true white can bring freshness to an outfit, but warmer whites like ivory, cream and ecru tend to create softer contrast.

That doesn't mean you have to abandon a bright white tee forever. If the fabric is dense enough and the fit is right, it can still look clean and sharp. But if you're shopping for the least-revealing option, a warmer white may be a smarter move than the blinding multipack version you bought on a whim.

articles.title: 'Old Person Smell' Is Real, And Science Will Dictate Whether It Happens To You
articles.summary: That musty smell could be more than just your old clothes, experts say.
articles.body:
Can you remember how your favorite grandma smelled? If you think back to a beloved elder, you might be able to summon up the memory of a scent that's been described as a blend of stale oil and musty cardboard. It might remind you of opening up old books or unpacking a box of vintage clothing. And while it's much more subtle than the sweaty body odor of youth, it's definitely noticeable and probably filed away in your memories as "old person smell."

As it turns out, that smell is an actual biological phenomenon, caused by an epidermal change that happens to everyone as they age. According to skin experts, every birthday after age 40 increases the likelihood of these changes in the way skin smells. Research has identified the culprit as something called 2-nonenal (pronounced noh-neh-nahl ), an organic compound known as an aldehyde.

That "aging odor" is caused by increased production of this aldehyde in older people, which is the source of a distinctive, dusty "granny" smell. Not all aldehydes smell the same, by the way, and another example is cinnamaldehyde, the organic compound that gives cinnamon its characteristic flavor and aroma, explained Dr. Delphine J. Lee , chief of dermatology and residency program director at Harbor-UCLA Medical Center.

We spoke with dermatologists and other experts to get to the bottom of why this happens.

Here's what changes in your skin to produce the scent.

The compound 2-nonenal has its own unique scent, and it proliferates as people get older. "As we age, several things happen simultaneously in our skin," said Dr. Sonal Choudhary , a dermatologist from the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine. "Antioxidant defenses in the skin decline, the composition of our sebum changes, and our cumulative UV exposure and environmental stress increase oxidative damage in the skin." As these things are weakening the skin, 2-nonenal has an opportunity to make its presence known.

"Research suggests measurable increases in 2-nonenal typically begin after age 40, with more noticeable accumulation in the 50s and beyond," Choudhary said. "It's a gradual process, not an instant switch. The intensity of the smell varies significantly from person to person depending on genetics, skin type, lifestyle and environmental exposure."

It's something that happens to most people, said dermatologist Dr. Naana Boakye , founder of Bergen Dermatology . "Evidence suggests that 2-nonenal production is a common age-related phenomenon, not something limited to a small subset of people," she noted. "Studies consistently detect this grassy, greasy scent in older adults of both sexes. While levels vary between individuals, there is no evidence that only certain people produce it."

You may not be able to smell it yourself if you're producing it.

Since so many factors, including genetics and lifestyle, contribute to the condition of your skin, you may get lucky and avoid the 2-nonenal odor altogether. And even if that distinctive smell does show up, remember that it's all in the nose of the beholder. "People can exaggerate that this smell is unpleasant or disgusting," Lee said. "It may even be more neutral or pleasant than the body odors of younger and middle-aged people."

As Choudhary mentioned, this process happens gradually, and that gives your brain an opportunity to become accustomed to the new scent, thanks to something called olfactory adaptation. You might not notice a prevalent scent after a while, since brains often filter out familiar odors, while staying alert for new information. An example of this "nose blindness" is that we might notice a friend's house always smells a certain way but are probably unable to detect our own home's unique scent.

Unlike sweat, it doesn't wash off easily.

Since 2-nonenal is a fatty acid, it won't easily dissolve in soap and water, the way sweat does. "It's hard to get rid of this molecule, because it's very sticky," said Danielle Reed , chief science officer at Monell Chemical Senses Center, a nonprofit research institute that studies taste and smell. "It loves to stick to your skin and it loves to stick to fabrics. You'll remove some of it when you bathe, but your body is constantly making it, so washing isn't a cure."

Boakye suggested it might be helpful to use antioxidant-based cleansers. She also said products with ingredients that bind aldehydes, like tannins, may help reduce odor persistence in some people. "Persimmon soap, which contains tannins, has a plausible mechanism and a long history of use, though large randomized trials are lacking," she noted. While none of these experts recommended specific products, Mirai's clinical persimmon soap , with Japanese persimmon and green tea extract, is popular and highly rated.

Recent research has looked at the potential role eggplant extract might play in reducing the oxidative stress that contributes to 2-nonenal formation. In a study published last year, researchers said the fruits, leaves, stems and roots of eggplant, along with their active ingredient N-trans-feruloylputrescine , exhibited excellent 2-nonenal scavenging activity. But that's a "someday" option, Lee said: "Human clinical data remain limited, so this should not be positioned as a cure."

An older study was initially positive about how the consumption of white button mushroom extract could alleviate body odor in subjects aged 50 to 79, but there have not been large clinical trials to follow up on that.

So there's still no sure-fire way to completely eliminate it from your skin, experts agreed. "If you could figure this out, you'd be very rich, but so far there's nothing that's truly helpful," Reed said.

And also? It's all natural and perfectly OK.

If you're noticing this scent on yourself or someone you love, don't be ashamed or judgmental. Choudhary noted that it's not a sign of poor hygiene, nor is it inevitable or unmanageable. "This is a normal biochemical change of aging skin, similar to wrinkles or dryness," she said. "With thoughtful skin care, antioxidant support and proper laundering, it can often be minimized significantly."

Another consideration is that smell is a subjective area for humans. "We've decided we don't like the odor of old people, but we love the odor of babies' heads," Reed said. "Perhaps, as a society, we could learn to love the smell of aging. Not everyone finds this smell unpleasant, and there's always something for everybody when it comes to smell."

There's also the opportunity to lean into this and other age-related changes, because they're going to happen whether we like them or not.

"As a dermatologist, I emphasize that aging is a natural, lifelong biological process experienced by us all," Lee said. "We should focus on promoting health and well-being across our lifespans, while recognizing and valuing the wisdom, resilience and lived experience that accompany advancing age. I'd like us to place less emphasis on cosmetic or physiological changes such as body odor or wrinkles, which are often part of a life fully lived."

The original version of this story was published on HuffPost at an earlier date.

articles.title: Don’t throw away your empty plastic bottles: turn one into a simple self-watering planter at home and keep your plants hydrated with this easy DIY trick
articles.summary: If you have an empty plastic bottle lying around at home, don’t throw it away just yet. With a few simple steps, you can turn it into a small self-wat.
articles.body: If you have an empty plastic bottle lying around at home, don’t throw it away just yet. With a few simple steps, you can turn it into a small self-watering planter for herbs, flowers or other small plants. Make a miniature self-watering planter out of a plastic bottle. This is a quick and easy DIY for repurposing a plastic bottle that will come in handy for growing herbs or flowers indoors.A self-watering planter is the easiest way to grow plants if you are not the most enthusiastic about taking care of them. It helps to keep the soil constantly moist without having to water the plants directly.Materials to use:A plastic bottleSharp scissors or a cutterPotting soilCotton or a thick stringWaterHerbs, flower seeds or any other plants that you want to growInstructionsPreparing the plastic bottle is also very important. Wash and dry the bottle before doing anything else.Cut the plastic bottle in halfCut the plastic bottle roughly in half to get two parts of it. It does not have to be in the middle but just leave enough space at the bottom to hold water and also room at the top to grow your plants.Make a water-wicking hole in the capMake a hole in the cap and tie a piece of cotton cord or a thick string. The thread should be thick enough to hold water. Make sure to leave enough of it on both sides. Screw the cap back on the bottle.The principle is similar to a regular self-watering pot. The cotton cord serves as a wick that transports water from the bottom reservoir up to the plant’s roots.Assemble the self-watering planterTake the top of the plastic bottle and insert it into the second part of the bottle. Make sure that the wick is facing the water reservoir. Add the potting soil to the top part of the plastic bottle. Make sure to fill it up to the wick. Do not make the soil compactedto provide ample space for the roots.Plant your desired plants on the planter.Fill the water tank and choose the appropriate location for your planter. The wick must be wet but not submerged in water. Put the planter where it can get the required amount of sunlight depending on what you will grow there. Self-watering planters need little care but remember to keep an eye on the water level and the condition of the soil.An effective and fast DIY projectThe planter from a plastic bottle is an excellent example of recycling and minimizing the use of plastic. It also looks charming on a windowsill or a balcony. However, even though the self-watering planter takes care of most of the plant needs, you should still check the condition of the roots and the soil occasionally and ensure that the plant is not sitting in too much water.Also read:Why your plant’s new leaves are smaller than the old ones: Signs to watch and simple ways to improve new growthDIY: Have an empty wall? This no-drill home décor hack can transform your space in just an afternoonWatch out for the plantEven though the wick is responsible for most of the water delivery, regular observation is still recommended. If the soil in the planter always seems moist and the plant looks sick, then you need to reduce the amount of water and let the soil get dry a little bit. Plants have various moisture requirements and some observation will help you understand how to balance the things.Personalize your new planterThere is also room for personalization here. You can paint the outside of the bottle, tie it with jute, or add some simple patterns. If you decide to make several such planters, then you can use different bottles for different herbs and label them. It is an easy project that can turn waste into a small indoor garden.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: Should You Ever Take “Beige Flags” Seriously? Here’s What Relationship Experts Say
articles.summary: Do these “neutral” signals really mean anything?
articles.body:
Beige flags can include behaviors like talking to oneself, keeping 40 tabs open on a computer, or having a strangely intense relationship with a fantasy football team.

While noticing beige flags can be playful, they aren't a particularly useful tool for determining the health of a relationship, as real relationships are built on emotional safety, shared values, communication, and consistency.

Anyone who has dated recently knows that it's tough out there. Not only are you getting to know someone's personality to see if you're compatible, but you're also on the lookout for traits or behaviors that give you pause—often referred to as " red flags ."

On the other hand, "green flags" are things about a person you're dating that are definite good signs, and indicate the potential for a healthy, loving relationship. You want those.

But there's another color flag that's been getting a lot of attention on social media lately: beige flags. So what, exactly, are beige flags, and what do they tell us about a potential partner? Here's what relationship experts and therapists have to say.

Beige flags are the quirky, unusual, or slightly boring traits you notice in someone that aren't necessarily good or bad, says Kimmy Seltzer, a dating expert. "They are more 'vanilla,'" she explains. "Unlike red flags, they don't signal danger, and unlike green flags, they don't automatically tell you this person is a great partner. They're simply the little behaviors that make you pause and think, 'Huh, that's interesting.'"

Sometimes the term also gets used for dating profiles that feel so basic they could belong to anyone, says Giulia P. Davis, LMFT , a licensed marriage and family therapist and the founder of Mycelia Therapy. "The term originally described dating profiles that were so generic—'I love to travel,' 'I'm fluent in sarcasm,' or 'My dog is my best friend'—that they revealed almost nothing about the person," Seltzer says. "It has since expanded to include the harmless peculiarities people discover once they start dating someone."

Debra Alper, LCSW , a therapist and divorce consultant, thinks the term caught on because people were burned out from red-flag culture. "Everyone got so used to scanning dates for danger signs that they started noticing most quirks aren't actually evidence of anything at all," she says. "Calling something 'beige' lets people notice it, maybe laugh about it, and then just keep going instead of turning every small habit into a referendum on the relationship."

Beige flags are interesting because they tell us less about the person we're observing and more about our own reaction to them, Davis says. "The important question is what you feel when you notice the trait," she notes.

Beige flags can come in many different forms. Remember, they're traits or behaviors that are neither good nor bad—just neutral or quirky. According to the experts we spoke with, some examples of beige flags include:

Quoting movie lines during serious conversations

Keeping a detailed spreadsheet ranking every restaurant they've visited

Watching the same television series repeatedly

Telling the same five stories at every social gathering

Having a strangely intense relationship with their fantasy football team

Refusing to use GPS because they "know a better way"

Owning an unusual amount of clothing in the same color

Having a ranking system for gas station coffee

Beige flags are the kinds of things you notice and possibly find weird without there necessarily being anything wrong with them, says Ann Parnes, a matchmaker at After Hello Matchmaking .

"The important distinction is that a beige flag may be odd, mildly annoying, or simply memorable, but it isn't inherently harmful," Seltzer says. "One person's beige flag might even be another person's most lovable quality."

Is looking for beige flags a healthy way to assess a relationship?

Beige flags can be a playful way to notice someone's personality, but they aren't a particularly useful tool for determining whether a relationship is healthy, Seltzer says. "Dating has become so focused on categorizing people and vetting people so hard that we sometimes treat every human imperfection as evidence that someone is incompatible with us," she explains. "A lot of times, that is a fear-based way of dating to try to ward off people and situations that happened in previous relationships and not true areas of concern."

Dating isn't supposed to feel like a background check, says Debra Stangl, relationship expert and author of High-Vibe Relationship: Why Love Isn't the Problem—and What Actually Is .

"A better question is: How does this person consistently make me feel? Safe? Respected? Seen? Valued? Can I be myself around them? That tells you far more than whether they collect vintage lunchboxes," she notes.

Along the same lines, Seltzer says that real relationships aren't built by finding someone with no strange habits. "They're built through emotional safety, shared values, communication, consistency, and the ability to work through differences," she says.

While noticing beige flags isn't an issue, Parnes says that the problem begins when we start giving these neutral qualities the same weight as the things that really do tell us something about whether someone will be a good partner. "Beige flags are part of what makes someone who they are, and some of those little things that seem strange or mildly annoying early on may eventually become the things you find most endearing about them," she explains.

According to Alper, approaching beige flags with "light curiosity" is a healthy approach. "Where it goes sideways is when beige-flag hunting becomes just another form of the same hypervigilance red-flag culture created in the first place," she explains. "Whether you're calling it red or green or beige, if you're combing every date for clues, you're usually chasing certainty way before the relationship has had time to actually produce any."

Instead of looking for and assessing beige flags, Alper would rather see people gather real information over a longer stretch—like how someone handles friction, how they talk about their exes, whether what they say lines up with what they do over weeks and months—not one dinner. "A beige flag is a single data point," she says. "It's not a verdict, and definitely not a dataset. Once you start treating every quirk like evidence to be logged and cross-referenced, you've stopped dating and started surveilling."

How to determine whether a beige flag should be a cause for concern

Everyone comes with imperfections and quirks. The question is whether you can overlook or live with a particular trait in the context of everything else that person brings to the relationship, Parnes says. "One person's harmless quirk can be another person's genuine incompatibility," she explains. "If someone bikes 100 miles a week, for example, that may be completely irrelevant to one partner and a significant lifestyle issue for another."

Stangl recommends asking yourself whether the beige flag is just quirky, or if it is affecting your connection with your partner. Is this something you can live with for the rest of your life, or is it going to drive you up the wall after 20 years? "If it's mildly annoying or eccentric, it's probably beige," she says. "If it repeatedly leaves you feeling controlled, dismissed, unsafe, unseen, or unable to communicate, it may not be beige at all."

It's also important to remember that you're not going to love every single thing about your partner. "Sometimes a beige flag is just another human being human," Stangl says.

Candidato ao Governo do Amazonas, David Almeida (Avante) visitou feirantes e apoiadores na Zona Sul de Manaus. — Foto: Rede Amazônica

O candidato ao governo do Amazonas, David Almeida (Avante), visitou feirantes e apoiadores no bairro Raiz, Zona Sul de Manaus , nesta terça-feira (1º). Durante a agenda, ele apresentou propostas para a educação e prometeu ampliar as vagas em escolas de tempo integral no estado.

Entre as propostas, reforçou a necessidade de aumentar a quantidade de vagas em escolas de tempo integral. O candidato também prometeu expandir a rede de creches para melhorar o acesso à educação infantil, com a oferta de novas vagas.

" Nós vamos fazer exatamente o que fizemos com Manaus. Nós tínhamos seis mil vagas em escolas de tempo integral, passamos para 22 mil vagas em escolas de tempo integral. Também melhoramos a questão do acesso a creche. A gente está formando melhores alunos para o Ensino Médio, mas não está dando sequência no governo do estado. Como governador, nós vamos mudar essa realidade e colocar o Amazonas no patamar que ele merece".

A agenda do candidato continuou pela tarde com uma entrevista a um portal de notícias local. Pela tarde, David Almeida participou de um almoço na comunidade Raio de Sol e de uma caminhada na Zona Norte da cidade. A noite, participou de uma reunião na comunidade Buritis.

articles.title: 'Vimos o nível da lama, quase 90%. Lá, nossa esperança acabou”, diz resgatista no Nepal | G1
articles.standfirst: Chegou a 1.066 o número de mortos pela avalanche no Nepal e no Tibete. As equipes ainda tentam encontrar sobreviventes dentro de usinas hidrelétricas soterradas pela enxurrada.
articles.summary: Chegou a 1.066 o número de mortos pela avalanche no Nepal e no Tibete. As equipes ainda tentam encontrar sobreviventes dentro de usinas hidrelétricas soterradas pela enxurrada.
articles.body:
Subiu para 1.066 o número de mortos pela avalanche no Nepal e no Tibete.

Por terra, água e ar. Os trabalhos no Himalaia avançam do jeito que dá. No escuro, o drone foi aonde os socorristas não conseguem chegar. As imagens são de um túnel de uma das mais de dez usinas hidrelétricas atingidas. Mas o equipamento não encontrou qualquer sinal de vida.

“Vimos o nível da lama, quase 90%. Lá, nossa esperança acabou”, disse o operador de drone.

Acredita-se que mais de 600 trabalhadores ainda estejam presos nas hidrelétricas. Socorristas especializados da Índia e da China ajudam nas buscas.

'Vimos o nível da lama, quase 90%. Lá, nossa esperança acabou”, diz resgatista no Nepal — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Um estudo divulgado por um grupo internacional de cientistas mostrou que, se a região tivesse um sistema de alerta adequado, muitas vidas poderiam ter sido salvas. Os pesquisadores também apontaram indícios de rachaduras em imagens de satélite da geleira e da encosta rochosa dias antes da avalanche.

Quase uma semana depois, as Nações Unidas destacam que o perigo ainda é enorme. Há riscos de novos deslizamentos e enchentes - e também de doenças. Faltam água, comida, atendimento médico. Direto do Nepal, em entrevista a jornalistas na ONU , o responsável pelas operações da Cruz Vermelha contou que um deslocamento que antes levava dez minutos agora pode levar nove horas.

O medo de mais inundação não impediu que centenas de pessoas caminhassem quilômetros para homenagear vítimas desconhecidas de uma tragédia comum.

articles.title: Peru rompe relações diplomáticas com Irã | G1
articles.standfirst: Governo peruano também criticou restrições à navegação no Estreito de Ormuz e situação da democracia e dos direitos humanos no país.
articles.summary: Governo peruano também criticou restrições à navegação no Estreito de Ormuz e situação da democracia e dos direitos humanos no país.
articles.body:
O Peru rompeu nesta terça-feira (1º) relações diplomáticas com o Irã . Segundo a chancelaria peruana, a decisão foi tomada diante da atuação de Teerã no Oriente Médio, das restrições à navegação no Estreito de Ormuz e de preocupações com a situação da democracia e dos direitos humanos no país.

Em comunicado, o governo peruano afirmou que condena a “escalada de conflitos” no Oriente Médio e acusou o Irã de incentivar a violência na região. A decisão foi tomada um mês após Keiko Fujimori assumir como presidente do país.

O Peru também criticou as “severas restrições” impostas pelo regime iraniano e a interrupção do comércio internacional pelo Estreito de Ormuz desde março de 2026.

Segundo o governo, as medidas violam princípios como a liberdade de navegação e o direito de passagem por estreitos usados no trânsito marítimo internacional.

A chancelaria peruana afirmou ainda que as restrições têm impacto sobre os preços da energia e a estabilidade das cadeias globais de abastecimento.

O Peru também criticou a atuação do Irã em relação ao programa nuclear. Segundo o governo peruano, Teerã tem dificultado o trabalho da Agência Internacional de Energia Atômica (AIEA) ao negar, em diferentes ocasiões, acesso de inspetores a instalações nucleares.

O governo peruano afirmou que a decisão de romper relações foi tomada com base em sua “histórica vocação pacifista” e no compromisso com o direito internacional e a defesa da democracia.

Segundo a chancelaria, a decisão foi comunicada ao Irã por meio de uma nota diplomática entregue pela Embaixada iraniana no Equador, que também atua como representação diplomática do país no Peru.

O Irã não havia se manifestado sobre a decisão até a última atualização desta reportagem.

A ex-candidata Keiko Fujimori, durante declaração à imprensa na qual anunciou que irá reconhecer o resultado das eleições presidenciais do Peru, em Lima, na segunda-feira (19) — Foto: Reuters/Sebastian Castaneda

articles.summary: Debate para o governo do DF reuniu seis candidatos que discutiram propostas para saúde e transporte em meio a trocas de acusações diretas entre Celina Leão e Ricardo Cappelli.
articles.body:
Candidatos ao governo do Distrito Federal participam de segundo debate — Foto: Correio Braziliense/Reprodução

Candidatos ao governo do Distrito Federal participaram nesta terça-feira (1º) do segundo debate eleitoral para a disputa de 2026 .

O evento foi promovido pelo Correio Braziliense e pela TV Brasília e reuniu seis candidatos ao Palácio do Buriti: Celina Leão (PP), José Roberto Arruda (PSD), Kiko Caputo (Novo), Leandro Grass (PT), Paula Belmonte (PSDB) e Ricardo Cappelli (PSB).

O encontro foi dividido em quatro blocos:

No primeiro bloco, candidatos responderam a perguntas de jornalistas do Correio Braziliense. Um outro candidato foi escolhido, em cada pergunta, para comentar.

No segundo bloco e no terceiro blocos, os candidatos fizeram perguntas entre si.

No quarto e ú, cada participante teve um minuto e meio para as considerações finais.

O debate desta terça foi marcado por embates mais diretos entre os candidatos, com troca de acusações e pedidos de resposta.

Assim como no debate anterior, promovido pela Band, os cinco outros candidatos usaram várias de suas participações para criticar o atual governo. Candidata à reeleição, Celina Leão (PP) "se defendeu" durante suas intervenções e classificou o evento como "caça à leoa".

Em uma das interações no terceiro bloco, Celina Leão chamou Cappelli de "bobo da corte do 8 de janeiro" – uma crítica à atuação de Cappelli como interventor federal na Segurança Pública df DF após os atos golpistas em 2023. Naquele momento, Ibaneis foi afastado do governo e Celina era governadora interina.

A direção do debate concedeu direito de resposta a Cappelli. O candidato usou os 45 segundos para dizer que "bobo da corte é a população do Distrito Federal que pega o ônibus lá em Brazlândia" – e voltou a "desafiar" Celina a pegar ônibus em algum terminal do DF.

Celina e Cappelli protagonizaram, ainda, um segundo embate. A candidata à reeleição acusou Cappelli de ter sido condenado por "violência de gênero" contra ela em uma propaganda política . Cappelli afirmou que Celina mentiu.

➡️ Como mostrou o g1 , a Justiça Eleitoral determinou que Cappelli apagasse os vídeos de suas redes sociais, mas a decisão foi derrubada após recurso do candidato . Na segunda decisão, o juiz disse que "não é possível concluir que a crítica foi dirigida à condição de mulher".

Nas considerações finais, Paula Belmonte acusou Celina Leão de estar usando dois celulares durante o evento – o que era proibido pelas regras do debate. Logo antes, a organização do debate já havia sinalizado aos candidatos que era proibido o uso de dispositivos eletrônicos.

Candidata ao governo do DF Paula Belmonte (PSDB) participa de segundo debate — Foto: Correio Braziliense/Reprodução

Primeira a responder, Paula Belmonte (PSDB) foi questionada sobre suas experiências anteriores de gestão, e o que a "credenciaria" a governar o Distrito Federal. A candidata afirmou que é administradora "por formação" e empresária, e que o governo atual "não sabe onde está colocando o dinheiro"

"Falta gestão, e é isso que nós queremos. Que a gente possa fazer uma boa gestão do nosso governo, a partir de 2027, e trazer a transparência e o combate à corrupção", declarou Paula.

Escolhida para comentar, Celina Leão (PP) disse acreditar que mostrou capacidade de gestão quando assumiu o governo – por exemplo, quando o então governador Ibaneis (MDB) foi afastado após os atos de 8 de janeiro.

Candidato ao governo do DF Leandro Grass (PT) participa de segundo debate — Foto: Correio Braziliense/Reprodução

O candidato Leandro Grass (PT) foi o sorteado para a segunda pergunta. Questionado sobre suposta posição contrária do PT ao Fundo Constitucional, Grass afirmou que negou ataques aos FCDF por parte do governo Lula.

Ele citou ainda medida aprovada no Congresso e contestada pela governadora Celina Leão que prevê renúncia de receita de combustíveis.

“Esse projeto não trata especificamente do Fundo, ele muda a forma de correção dos fundos de maneira geral e não há redução, há apenas uma mudança no cálculo de incremento, que pode ser ainda ajustado e alterado”, afirmou.

Escolhido para comentar a resposta, José Roberto Arruda (PSD) afirmou que o governo do DF vive um momento de “falta de credibilidade” e que “perdeu a capacidade de diálogo com o Congresso e com o governo federal”.

Candidato ao governo do DF Ricardo Cappelli (PSB) participa de segundo debate — Foto: Correio Braziliense/Reprodução

Em seguida, Ricardo Cappelli (PSB) foi questionado sobre estratégias para a segurança pública.

O candidato disse que vai contratar 7 mil policiais militares pra preencher o déficit atual, voltar com a estratégia "Cosme e Damião" de patrulhamento de rua e com rondas ostensivas, além de combater o feminicídio.

Indicado para comentar o tema, Kiko Caputo (Novo) afirmou que a segurança pública será prioridade em seu eventual governo e que, em vez de "olhar para o passado", pretende investir em tecnologia até conseguir repor o contingente da PM.

Candidato ao governo do DF José Roberto Arruda (PSD) participa de segundo debate — Foto: Correio Braziliense/Reprodução

Quarto a responder, Arruda (PSD) foi perguntado sobre suas soluções para a crise do Banco Master. Disse que o BRB foi "assaltado" e que os R$ 16 bilhões retirados do banco seriam suficientes para construir 35 hospitais públicos.

Afirmou, ainda, que pretende fechar as agências do BRB fora de Brasília, revisar os acordos de patrocínio e abrir um Plano de Demissão Voluntária para reduzir o número de servidores.

Chamado a comentar a resposta, Leandro Grass (PT) disse ter um compromisso de combater irregularidades e ser ficha limpa.

Candidato ao governo do DF Kiko Caputo (NOVO) participa de segundo debate — Foto: Correio Braziliense/Reprodução

Quinto no sorteio, Kiko Caputo (Novo) foi perguntado sobre o foco de sua proposta econômica, incluindo possíveis privatizações. Kiko disse que, quando começar a gerir "de forma proba e honesta", vai sobrar dinheiro nos cofres públicos para ações como recuperar o Metrô e dar um "choque de transparência".

Chamada a comentar, Paula Belmonte (PSDB) também criticou o governo atual e a privatização da CEB e da gestão da rodoviária.

Candidata ao governo do DF Celina Leão (PP) participa de segundo debate — Foto: Correio Braziliense/Reprodução

Última a ser questionada, Celina Leão (PP) foi questionada sobre dois problemas que a próxima gestão terá de resolver: a possível redução do Fundo Constitucional e a dívida do BRB.

Em resposta, Celina disse que assumiu o governo com duas grandes crises e "não correu dos problemas". Afirmou, ainda, que o BRB vai conseguir pagar o empréstimo que está sendo negociado com as próprias receitas.

Ao comentar a resposta, Cappelli (PSB) afirmou que o governo de Celina "comandou a roubalheira no BRB e agora quer tomar um empréstimo para você [espectador] pagar o rombo". E que fará diferente, se for eleito.

No início das perguntas diretas, Arruda (PSD) questionou Celina Leão (PP) sobre as críticas feitas pela adversária na propaganda eleitoral e o pedido de impugnação de sua chapa.

Em resposta, Celina disse que as críticas são políticas, e não à pessoa. E defendeu ações que tomou desde que assumiu o governo, em maio, como a contratação de 20 mil consultas. "Eu sou a candidata mais atacada, alguns candidatos aqui já foram até condenados por violência de gênero contra a minha pessoa", disse.

Na réplica, Arruda questionou se Celina Leão não viu os problemas da saúde e a crise do BRB enquanto era vice-governadora. E disse que a única ação da governadora na saúde foi "inaugurar uma cerca". Celina rebateu as críticas na tréplica.

Celina Leão voltou a falar sobre o projeto de renúncia fiscal com Leandro Grass . A governadora acusou o partido do candidato de tentar acabar com o Fundo Constitucional. “Como o senhor, no seu governo, vai agir? O senhor vai entrar na justiça também para defender o fundo constitucional?”, questionou a candidata à reeleição.

Grass voltou a afirmar que o governo Lula aumentou o valor do fundo. O candidato afirmou que a adversária teve a oportunidade de entregar a melhor educação e segurança pública do Brasil. “Sabe o que você está entregando? Você está entregando o último lugar no Ideb. Você está entregando o maior tempo de espera para exames e cirurgias”, afirmou.

“Você fala que não era a governadora, que era o Ibaneis. Você estava em que lugar? Onde é que você trabalhava? Você trabalha em outro prédio, em outro governo? Você caiu no GDF de uma hora para outra, de paraquedas? Você não foi eleita na chapa do Ibaneis?”, questionou.

A governadora rebateu as acusações e voltou a falar de ameaças ao Fundo. “O governo federal, quando ele não consegue ajustar as contas, ele aumenta imposto. Agora ele quer mexer nos fundos constitucionais, quer mexer sim, está comprovado e nós fomos ao judiciário”, afirmou.

Em seguida, Kiko Caputo (Novo) questionou Cappelli (PSB) sobre a piora do DF em indicadores sociais de saúde e educação, como o Índice de Desenvolvimento da Educação Básica (Ideb).

Em resposta, Cappelli disse que há moradores do DF indo para cidades do Entorno para fazer tratamentos de saúde, e que pretende lançar o programa Fila Zero para extinguir a fila de espera por consultas, procedimentos e cirurgias na rede pública.

Ao retomar a palavra, Kiko Caputo afirmou que o DF é a unidade da Federação que mais gasta com saúde por pessoa no país, e que "o dinheiro está indo para o ralo da corrupção enquanto você está vendo pessoas morrendo nas filas sem atendimento".

Ricardo Cappelli questionou Paula Belmonte sobre projetos para a saúde . O candidato destacou o tempo de espera nas Unidades de Pronto-Atendimento (UPA).

Na réplica, Belmonte afirmou que “a saúde pública do Distrito Federal não está só em UTI, ela está já entubada”.

“O governo que deixou a saúde chegar onde chegou esse é o governo que deixou o BRB acontecer o que tá acontecendo, que não atende as pessoas e está usando de populismo para fazer ação agora em quatro meses”, afirmou. A candidata destacou ainda que, se eleita, vai investir na saúde primária.

Cappelli voltou a mencionar a criação do Fila Zero. O candidato afirma que vai zerar as filas da saúde com a contratação de profissionais e conclusão das obras de hospitais.

Em seguida, Leandro Grass (PT) perguntou a Kiko Caputo (Novo) sobre a escolha do candidato a vice-governador e o papel que ele teria em um eventual governo.

Kiko disse ter escolhido um "servidor público exemplar da segurança pública, ex-líder classista" e voltou a falar em choque de gestão.

Kiko e Grass usaram a pergunta para criticar Celina Leão, ex-vice-governadora de Ibaneis e atual governadora.

Última do bloco, Paula Belmonte perguntou a Arruda sobre a crise do BRB . Os dois candidatos também usaram o tema para criticar o governo atual, a quem atribuíram a crise.

"O que nos compete hoje é tirar esse pano de cima do problema do BRB, estampar a realidade para a sociedade e, juntos, discutimos uma solução. O FCO [Fundo do Centro-Oeste] pode ser uma solução. O fundo do Nordeste é aplicado no Banco do Nordeste. O FCO pode ser aplicado no BRB", disse Arruda.

"Como é que você vai votar em um candidato que está escondendo da sociedade o balanço do BRB? Não temos condições de votar em quem está escondendo. Eu peço: botem na rede o balanço do BRB, deixe as pessoas saberem o que está acontecendo de verdade", rebateu Paula.

As filas na saúde também foram tema no debate entre Celina e Arruda . Em pergunta, a candidata à reeleição lembrou programa feito na gestão do ex-governador – e disse que a iniciativa não atingiu o resultado esperado.

“O problema da saúde pública é um problema que a gente enfrenta há muitos mandatos, inclusive da época do senhor. O que o senhor pensa em fazer de novo que o senhor não fez na época que o senhor era governador?”, perguntou.

Arruda afirmou que, durante o mandato dele, as unidades de saúde contavam com especialistas. Ele afirmou ainda que construiu o Hospital de Santa Maria. “Passaram 16 anos, vocês não deram conta de construir mais nenhum hospital”, afirmou.

“Como a senhora copia todas as ideias que eu dou, por que a senhora não nomeia logo todos os profissionais da saúde concursados? Quem sabe ameniza um pouquinho a dor das pessoas”, declarou Arruda.

Em seguida, Cappelli perguntou a Celina Leão sobre o tempo gasto pelos moradores do DF no transporte público . E "convidou" Celina a ir para as rodoviárias do DF no início da manhã.

Celina respondeu dizendo que o transporte público é prioridade do governo atual e que há estudos e investimentos em andamento para expansões do Metrô e para o BRT Norte. A governadora disse ainda que, se reeleita, fará um estudo para implementar o tarifa zero.

Na réplica, Cappelli repetiu uma de suas promessas: de que, se eleito, não haverá viagens de transporte público no DF que levem mais de uma hora. Em resposta, Celina criticou a gestão do ex-governador Rodrigo Rollemberg (PSB), do mesmo partido de Cappelli.

Paula Belmonte questionou Leandro Grass sobre propostas para a educação. Grass, que é professor de formação, destacou a importância das escolas em tempo integral.

O candidato falou ainda sobre a valorização dos profissionais da educação e prometeu que, se eleito, vai investir na contratação de professores efetivos.

“Eu vou nomear e diminuir essa quantidade de temporários que vão e voltam para a escola, mas não conseguem permanecer. Isso consta no projeto para a própria escola, para a gente ter nas famílias a oportunidade de o filho ficar em um local seguro”, afirmou.

Belmonte mencionou as filas das creches. “As nossas crianças nascem sem uma continuidade de educação. Precisamos que os professores tenham vínculos e as mães de crianças atípicas se sintam seguras para colocar o seu filho na escola”, declarou.

Quarto a perguntar, Arruda escolheu Kiko Caputo e perguntou sobre soluções para o transporte público.

Durante a interação, Arruda e Kiko listaram diversas obras de expansão do Metrô e de vias rápidas que pretendem fazer, se forem eleitos.

Kiko citou linhas de metrô ligando Samambaia, Pôr do Sol e Sol Nascente, BRT para a região Norte e quatro estradas-parque. E afirmou que os ônibus com ar-condicionado comprados pelo governo atual foram concentrados apenas nas linhas do Plano Piloto.

Já Arruda afirmou que, quando foi governador, não pagava subsídio às empresas de ônibus e que o governo atual vem enviando bilhões aos empresários do setor. E disse que o transporte sobre trilhos é "a única solução para Brasília voltar a ter uma mobilidade urbana".

Leandro Grass questionou Ricardo Cappelli sobre propostas para ocupação da Residência Oficial de Águas Claras , que não chegou a ser ocupada pelo governo atual.

Cappelli utilizou o tempo para propor projetos para educação e mobilidade urbana, mas não respondeu diretamente à pergunta do adversário. Ele afirmou que, se efeito, vai zerar as nomeações pendentes de concursados na educação e aumentar o salário dos professores. Ele destacou ainda a contratação de monitores para acompanhamento de crianças com autismo nas escolas.

O candidato do PT voltou a falar sobre a desocupação de prédios públicos. “No meu governo, eu vou pegar os equipamentos GDF que estão obsoletos e vou colocar na mão da sociedade. Vou transformar em equipamento público”, declarou.

Grass prometeu ainda que vai criar um centro de referência para cuidar de famílias atípicas: a gente vai ter equipamento público para servir a população, não para ficar lá às moscas, empoeirado, enquanto gastam bilhões de reais com aluguéis do governo.

Fechando o bloco, Kiko Caputo perguntou a Paula Belmonte sobre problemas na saúde pública.

Paula afirmou que o Iges-DF, que gerencia unidades de saúde, tem contratos emergenciais em vigor há mais de cinco anos e que "não tem rabo preso" com esse modelo.

"Atacar, sim, a máfia da saúde, a máfia da cirurgia, a máfia da prótese. É uma vergonha as pessoas passarem pelo que estão passando", afirmou.

Na réplica, Kiko disse que é preciso aumentar o horário de funcionamento das UBSs, construir quatro novos hospitais e transformar o hospital de Ceilândia em um hospital da mulher e materno-infantil. Defendeu que sejam contratadas 200 novas equipes do Saúde da Família.

Os candidatos tiveram um minuto e meio, cada, para as considerações finais. Os seis usaram o tempo para defender o próprio currículo e repetir promessas que já haviam sido listadas ao longo do debate, em áreas como saúde e educação.

articles.title: Meet Remya Jose: The 14-year-old Kerala girl who built a pedal-powered washing machine without electricity to save time for her board exams and earned a National Award from President APJ Abdul Kalam for it
articles.summary: Some of the best inventions don't come out of a lab. They come out of pure, everyday necessity. While most of us continue living with just ordinary pr.
articles.body: Some of the best inventions don't come out of a lab. They come out of pure, everyday necessity. While most of us continue living with just ordinary problems, someone decides not to.That's exactly what happened in a small village in Kerala's Malappuram district, where a 14-year-old girl named Remya Jose looked at hours of hand-washed laundry piling up on her already exhausting school schedule and decided to ‘build’ a machine instead of accepting the chore!She had no electricity to depend on, no money for a store-bought washing machine, and no engineering background, but something that pushed her ahead was pure curiosity, driven by need.Meet Reema Jose, the 14-year-old Kerala girl who built a non-electric washing machine using a bicycleRemya Jose was 14 years old and in her 10th standard, the year of India's board exams in 2005, when her situation took a hard turn. Her mother fell ill, and her father was undergoing cancer treatment. That left the household's laundry to be done by hand by Remya and her twin sister, on top of a school commute that already consumed nearly four hours a day changing three buses, according to the National Innovation Foundation of India report.Tired and pressed for time, Remya didn't just wish for a washing machine her family couldn't afford. She decided to build one. "Necessity is the mother of invention," she later said, describing how she studied the way an electric washing machine works and set out to recreate its function without electricity.How did she build the non-electric washing machine?After studying how a washing machine works, she realised that after stripping away the motor, a washing machine is really just a perforated drum spinning in soapy water. The motor's only job is to make it spin, and a bicycle already turns pedaling into rotation. So she sketched a design, with an aluminium cabin, a wire-mesh cylinder to hold the clothes, and a bicycle's chain, sprockets and pedals rigged up to turn the drum.Her father carried the sketch to a nearby automobile workshop, where mechanics agreed to build it in their spare time, using materials bought to Remya's specifications for around 2,000 rupees. The finished machine worked in three simple stages: soak the clothes in soapy water for about ten minutes, pedal for three to four minutes to scrub them clean, then drain, refill, and pedal again to rinse. A final round of pedaling with the water drained turns the drum into a centrifuge, wringing the clothes out to around 80 percent dryness.Her design was later taken as a patent and earned recognition from the presidentHer father initially doubted the project, thinking that a girl would eventually need to know how to wash clothes by hand regardless of any machine. Her mother, too, worried the project was distracting Remya from her studies, until the invention proved itself.The National Innovation Foundation, which scouts grassroots inventors through the Honey Bee Network, filed a patent on the design in 2003 and formally registered it as the "Washing Cum Exercise Machine."The invention got Remya a National Award, presented by then-President A.P.J. Abdul Kalam. She didn't stop there, either. She went on to work with the NIF as an innovator, developing further devices for rural households.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: Quote of the Day by Leo Tolstoy, "When you love someone, you love the person as they are, and not as you'd....”
articles.summary: Few writers have explored the human heart with the intensity, honesty and philosophical depth of Leo Tolstoy. His novels were vast in scale, filled wi.
articles.body: Few writers have explored the human heart with the intensity, honesty and philosophical depth of Leo Tolstoy. His novels were vast in scale, filled with wars, families, marriages, social upheaval and political change, yet at their centre were deeply personal questions. Born into Russian aristocracy, Tolstoy grew up surrounded by privilege, but spent much of his life questioning the very values of the society into which he had been born. He became one of the greatest novelists in world literature, but his influence extended far beyond fiction. His ideas on non-violence, morality, simplicity and resistance to injustice influenced thinkers and political leaders across the world, most famously Mahatma Gandhi.From aristocratic beginnings to literary greatnessLeo Tolstoy was born on September 9, 1828, at Yasnaya Polyana, his family's estate south of Moscow. He belonged to an old Russian aristocratic family and inherited the privileges associated with that social position. But Tolstoy's childhood was marked by loss. His mother died when he was very young, followed by his father a few years later. He was raised largely by relatives and servants alongside his siblings.As a young man, Tolstoy entered Kazan University but did not complete his studies. He returned to his family's estate and struggled to find direction. He experimented with different ways of living and began keeping the diaries that would remain an important part of his life.His early years were filled with contradictions. He enjoyed the privileges of an aristocrat while simultaneously becoming increasingly uncomfortable with the emptiness he saw in his own life. That tension would become one of the defining themes of his writing.The soldier who became a writerTolstoy's life took another turn when he joined the Russian army. His experiences during military service exposed him to violence, death and the realities of war. He served in the Caucasus and later during the Crimean War. These experiences became important material for his early fiction. His first major literary success came with Childhood, published in 1852. It was followed by Boyhood and Youth, completing a semi-autobiographical trilogy. Tolstoy quickly established himself as a major new voice in Russian literature.His writing was different from conventional romantic fiction. He was intensely interested in ordinary human behaviour-the small gestures, private doubts, selfish impulses, jealousies, disappointments and moments of tenderness that shape people's lives. He did not simply want to tell readers what his characters did. He wanted them to understand why they did it.‘War and Peace’: A world in one novelTolstoy's greatest achievement, War and Peace, was published in book form in the late 1860s. The novel is enormous in both size and ambition. Set during the Napoleonic Wars, it follows aristocratic families and individuals whose lives become entangled with the upheavals of history. Yet calling it simply a "war novel" would be misleading. Tolstoy combines romance, family drama, philosophy, politics and history. He moves between the battlefield and the drawing room, between soldiers and aristocrats, between private decisions and events involving entire nations. One of the novel's most important ideas is that history is not shaped solely by supposedly great men. Tolstoy questioned the idea that figures such as Napoleon single-handedly create history. Instead, he suggested that millions of individual actions, circumstances and social forces combine to produce historical change.This was revolutionary in its scope. Tolstoy was interested in the relationship between individual freedom and forces beyond human control, a question that would continue to occupy him throughout his life.‘Anna Karenina’ and the complexity of loveTolstoy followed War and Peace with another masterpiece, Anna Karenina, first published as a serial in the 1870s. The novel begins with marriage, desire and social expectations but gradually becomes a profound examination of human relationships. Anna's story explores passion, jealousy, social judgement and the devastating consequences of seeking fulfilment outside the boundaries imposed by society. Alongside Anna's story is the quieter journey of Konstantin Levin, whose struggles with work, faith, family and the meaning of existence closely reflected Tolstoy's own philosophical concerns.One of Tolstoy's greatest strengths was his refusal to divide people neatly into heroes and villains. His characters are contradictory because human beings themselves are contradictory. People can be generous and selfish, loving and cruel, courageous and frightened, all within the same life.The spiritual crisis that changed TolstoyDespite his extraordinary literary success, Tolstoy experienced a profound spiritual and existential crisis in middle age. He had fame, wealth, family and intellectual achievement, yet he became increasingly troubled by a fundamental question: What is the meaning of life if everyone eventually dies?His crisis led him to rethink almost everything he had previously accepted. He began rejecting materialism, excessive wealth and social privilege. He became increasingly critical of organised religion, the state, violence and institutions that he believed encouraged inequality and suffering. His transformation did not happen overnight. It was an intense, lifelong struggle. In A Confession, Tolstoy described this period of spiritual questioning. He increasingly came to believe that a meaningful life required compassion, moral responsibility, simplicity and love for others.Tolstoy's philosophy of non-violenceTolstoy's later writings became increasingly philosophical and political. He argued that violence could not ultimately create a moral society. Instead, he advocated resistance to evil through non-violence and moral courage. His ideas attracted readers around the world. Among them was Gandhi, who corresponded with Tolstoy and was deeply influenced by his writings on non-violence and moral resistance. Their exchange helped strengthen ideas that would later become central to Gandhi's philosophy and political practice.Tolstoy's influence was therefore not confined to literature. His ideas entered debates about pacifism, social justice, religion, political authority and ethical living.A writer who questioned his own privilegePerhaps one of the most remarkable things about Tolstoy was that he did not spare himself from the criticism he directed at society. He belonged to the privileged class he increasingly questioned. He owned a large estate and had servants, wealth and social status, yet he became increasingly uncomfortable with this way of life. He attempted to simplify his existence and became interested in manual labour. This contradiction remained unresolved.His contribution to literatureTolstoy transformed the possibilities of the novel. His greatest contribution was perhaps his extraordinary understanding of human psychology. His characters do not merely perform actions; readers experience their thoughts, doubts, rationalisations and emotional conflicts. He also changed the way writers could portray history. Instead of presenting historical events as the actions of a handful of powerful individuals, he examined the countless human decisions and social circumstances behind them. His influence can be seen across world literature, from psychological fiction to historical novels and family dramas. More than a century after his death, War and Peace and Anna Karenina remain among the most widely read works of literature.But Tolstoy's influence is not limited to his books. His essays, letters, diaries and philosophical writings continue to be studied because they reveal a mind constantly examining its own beliefs. Tolstoy's later life became increasingly complicated. His radical ideas created tension within his family, particularly with his wife, Sophia Tolstaya, with whom he had a long and difficult marriage. In his final years, Tolstoy became increasingly determined to abandon the privileges and possessions that conflicted with his ideals. In 1910, at the age of 82, he secretly left his home, hoping to begin a simpler life away from the conflicts surrounding him. During the journey, he became seriously ill. He died on November 20, 1910, at the railway station of Astapovo. His death became an international event, reflecting the extraordinary stature he had achieved.Quote of the day“When you love someone, you love the person as they are, and not as you'd like them to be.”This quote captures one of the most difficult truths about love: real love is not the same as loving an ideal version of someone. It is easy to love people when they behave exactly as we want them to. The challenge begins when we discover their flaws, their habits that irritate us, their weaknesses, their fears, their mistakes and the parts of their personality we wish were different.Tolstoy's idea suggests that love cannot be built entirely around expectations. If we love someone only because we hope they will change, we may not actually be loving the person—we may be loving a version of them that exists primarily in our imagination.To love someone "as they are" does not mean accepting everything they do without question. Love does not require tolerating cruelty, disrespect or harmful behaviour. Rather, it means recognising the difference between loving a person and trying to redesign them.There is an important distinction between acceptance and approval.You can wish someone would grow while still accepting who they are today. You can disagree with them without denying their humanity. You can see their flaws clearly and still recognise their worth. That may be why the idea remains so powerful.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: Bus gang-rape case: At minor’s UP village, locked house, silence and a family fleeing intrusion
articles.summary: Family of a 17-year-old survivor in the Noida-Delhi bus gang-rape case leaves their Mainpuri village, locking home amid media intrusion; two accused arrested.
articles.body: AGRA: Fearing intrusion and social stigma, parents of the 17-year-old survivor in the Noida-Delhi bus gang-rape case have locked their house and left their UP village.A villager, who knows the family, told TOI on Tuesday: “After media persons began visiting our remote village in Mainpuri district seeking details about that horrific incident, they couldn’t take it anymore.” He added: “There’s no one in that house now, the dwelling has fallen silent.”Another neighbour added: “No one here knew what had happened to the girl. When media persons came here on Monday and told us that she had been raped, everyone was shocked.” He appealed to journalists to avoid repeatedly visiting the place, citing concerns over the survivor’s future and privacy.“Please don’t come again and again to shoot videos or take pictures. She will have to get married in future. By revealing the village and asking people about her, the media has made the matter known here and also the neighbouring areas,” he added.The girl was allegedly sexually assaulted on a moving bus by the vehicle’s driver and conductor on Aug 4. The bus had travelled almost 50 km from Greater Noida to Old Delhi’s Kashmere Gate without being detected. The alleged sexual assault took place while she was travelling from Greater Noida towards Sector 63, police said.After violating her, the bus driver and conductor allegedly dumped her at Ring Road in the Kashmere Gate police station area. The accused duo were later identified as Kuldeep, 39 (bus driver); and Sandeep, 26 (conductor).The area’s SHO told TOI: “The family is safe and have gone to their relatives.”Local MLA, who visited the village on Monday, said, “People in the village came to know about it probably yesterday. When I went there, I found her house locked. Her father’s phone was switched off. I made considerable efforts to speak with the family, but I have been unable to do so thus far.”The MLA added: “I demand the strictest possible punishment for the two accused.” Meanwhile, president of UP State Women Commission, Babita Chauhan, has written to police commissioner of Gautam Budh Nagar for “tough action”.(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Agra | Silver Rate in Agra | Bank Holidays in Agra | Public Holidays in Agra | Agra AQI | Weather in Agra | Petrol Price in Agra | Diesel Price in Agra | CNG Price in Agra | LPG Price in AgraStay updated with the latest Agra news.
